title.narrative: Support for the Pacific Islands legal Information Institute (PacLII)

description.narrative: PacLII will support the provision of free access to legal information in the Pacific Islands and thereby help to ensure that the legal systems of all Pacific nations operate effectively and efficiently. The funding will support access to justice and enable the rule of law in the region- an important to Australia’s interests in the Pacific.

participating-org.narrative: AUSTRALIA - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: The Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute (PacLII), managed by the University of the South Pacific (USP) School of Law and Social Sciences, provides free online access to Pacific Islands laws via its website, averaging 1.4 million hits per month. Through this program, Australia contributed to the continuation and expansion of this key resource to the region. Focusing on in-country capacity building to strengthen document preparation for online publication, PacLII achieved its goal to increase its database contents. In 2024-2025, PacLII made available an additional 4,042 court decisions; and 1,869 pieces of legislation and government gazettes from 12 Pacific Island countries. The ability for all citizens to freely access current, accurate laws is essential to the rule of law and good governance in the Pacific.
